turns.en: Okay, we're here in the studio with special guest Jacob Lauritzen, CTO of Lora. Did I get it right?
turns.zh: 好的，我们正在演播室，特邀嘉宾是 Lora 的 CTO Jacob Lauritzen。我念对了吗？

turns.en: Lorisen is fine. Yeah, that's okay. I know how it is in Danish. Yeah, exactly.
turns.zh: Lorisen 就行。对，没问题。我知道丹麦语怎么念。对，没错。

turns.en: Does it have a special history?
turns.zh: 这个名字有什么特别的来历吗？

turns.en: Yeah, just know Sen is like son, son of. You have son, and yeah, so son of Lords. That's my name.
turns.zh: 有，Sen 就是儿子的意思，某某之子。你有 son，对，所以就是 Lords 之子。这就是我的名字。

turns.en: Nice. We've crossed paths here and there. You spoke at a few events, and obviously Lora is one of the fastest growing legal tech companies in history.
turns.zh: 不错。我们之前也碰过几次面。你在几个活动上演讲过，而且显然 Lora 是史上增长最快的法律科技公司之一。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And you said something at the start in a pre-show that I thought was really interesting. You said that your origin is very European, even though obviously you're expanding in New York and SF. What feels different about your culture?
turns.zh: 你在开场前说了一件我觉得很有意思的事。你说你们的起源非常欧洲，尽管你们显然正在纽约和旧金山扩张。你们的文化感觉有什么不同？

turns.en: I think we are just at the core probably very humble about what we're doing because we've always been the underdog from the very very beginning. No one believed that small startup in a basement in Stockholm was going to outcompete this huge company that was way ahead of us in the US. So I think we've always been underdogs and so we've always been very humble. We've always sort of had to fight for our existence. I think it's something we've had to learn as we've also become more and more, as we've entered the US and been in the US a lot more, is to be a little bit more bold and tell the world how great we are, because it doesn't come naturally to I think some of us.
turns.zh: 我觉得我们骨子里可能对所做的事非常谦逊，因为我们从一开始就一直是弱势的一方。没人相信斯德哥尔摩地下室里的小创业公司能打败美国那家远远领先于我们的巨头。所以我觉得我们一直是弱者，因此一直非常谦逊。我们一直都得为生存而战。我觉得随着我们越来越壮大、进入美国并在美国待得更多，我们不得不学会的一件事是稍微更大胆一些，告诉世界我们有多棒，因为这对我们中的一些人来说并不是自然而然的。

turns.en: I kind of want to start by going over your guys' product because I feel like with a lot of these legal products, they're kind of under wraps, you know, you're not supposed to show it. But if you could just talk about what does the product look like and maybe how did you guys get there? Like what have been the product iterations that got you to where you are today? I think that would be really interesting.
turns.zh: 我想先聊聊你们的产品，因为我觉得很多这类法律产品都挺神秘的，你知道，不该展示出来。但你能不能讲讲产品长什么样，也许你们是怎么走到今天的？比如哪些产品迭代让你们达到了今天的位置？我觉得那会很有意思。

turns.en: Yeah, absolutely. The way everything started was ChatGPT with a Swedish laws search tool in it. That was literally the entire everything. And so that's where we started. We started with legal research which is like a huge market basically in the world where lawyers spend a lot of time figuring out what are previous cases that look like this, what's the legal precedent like, what have previous people done in these situations. That's extremely important. And so that has always been part of our product. Basically we started from an agent you could ask questions and it would query laws. That was the very simple beginning. And then from that it's expanded. And so it's expanded in what can the agent do. It will now draft a lot of stuff really well. It will edit Word files. It will move your files away, organize everything. Run really complex analysis. And we've added just a bunch more features to it. So, one of our features called tabular view, which is now a name that's being used in industry, and we're very happy to see Claude for Legal using our terminology, what they're building.
turns.zh: 是的，当然。一切的开端就是 ChatGPT 里加了一个瑞典法律搜索工具。那就是全部了。所以我们就从那里开始。我们从法律研究做起，这基本上是世界上一个巨大的市场，律师花大量时间弄清楚之前有哪些类似的案例、法律先例是什么样的、以前的人在这些情况下是怎么做的。这极其重要。所以这一直是我们产品的一部分。基本上我们从一个你可以提问、它会查询法律的智能体开始。那是非常简单的起点。然后从那里扩展。所以它扩展到了智能体能做什么。它现在能很好地起草很多东西。它能编辑 Word 文件。它能移动你的文件、整理一切。运行非常复杂的分析。我们还给它加了一大堆功能。所以，我们的一个功能叫表格视图，现在这个名称已经在行业里被使用了，我们很高兴看到 Claude for Legal 在用我们的术语，他们正在构建的东西。

turns.en: We got to talk about that. We got to talk about that.
turns.zh: 我们得聊聊那个。我们得聊聊那个。

turns.en: Which is actually a way to just bulk extract and bulk review many, many, many agreements which you do in due diligence or when you raise money or whatever. So that's part of it is like we help lawyers just do their work much more efficiently, much much better. And then outside of just doing the work, we're also now helping orchestrate the work a lot more than we were just even a year ago. So we have different sort of—we have a thing called Lists which is sort of like Linear for us. And we have Intake which is a way to collaborate with clients. And we have Portal which is also sort of a way to collaborate, you know, lawyer to lawyer, client to lawyer, lawyer to agent, agent to agent maybe. We're spending a lot of time there because frankly the way that you work with a lawyer 10 years ago or maybe even today is really painful and there's loads of room to do that in a much better way to be honest. And so those are like I think the two things. It's doing the work and it's also orchestrating the work.
turns.zh: 这实际上就是一种批量提取和批量审阅大量协议的方式，你在尽职调查或融资等场景中会这么做。所以这部分就是我们帮助律师更高效、更好地完成工作。然后除了做工作本身，我们现在还比一年前更多地帮助协调工作。所以我们有不同种类的——我们有一个叫 Lists 的东西，对我们来说有点像 Linear。我们还有 Intake，这是一种与客户协作的方式。我们还有 Portal，这也是一种协作方式，你知道，律师对律师、客户对律师、律师对智能体、也许智能体对智能体。我们花了很多时间在那里，因为坦率地说，10 年前甚至今天与律师合作的方式真的很痛苦，说实话，有很大的空间可以做得更好。所以我觉得就是这两件事：做工作，以及协调工作。

turns.en: When did you guys start doing or building the agent?
turns.zh: 你们什么时候开始做或构建智能体的？

turns.en: So I mean we've basically had this switch from the assistant to the agent we call it, right.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，我们基本上经历了从助手到我们所谓的智能体的转变，对吧。

turns.en: I guess the agent—I don't know—I want to say a year ago probably.
turns.zh: 我猜智能体——我不知道——我想说大概一年前。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: So this is a rough timeline for people who are understanding YC 2023.
turns.zh: 所以这是一个粗略的时间线，给了解 YC 2023 的人。

turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And then you were a YC founder.
turns.zh: 然后你是 YC 创始人。

turns.en: YC 24.
turns.zh: YC 24。

turns.en: Yeah. I was in YC 23. The Goro was 24.
turns.zh: 对。我是 YC 23 的。Goro 是 24。

turns.en: Okay. And then so there is this is like a little bit pre—like agents really taking off and then like reasoning models obviously change everything. I mean you know in one sense today—you know we had a preview of the product—it does look well—preview we had a private thing but we will put up a video on YouTube—it's mostly like ChatGPT for lawyers, right? Like very fair to say that. But then the sidebar has a lot of nice custom tools like the tabular view, like the Intake which I really liked, and you know a bunch of other things.
turns.zh: 好的。然后所以这有点像在智能体真正起飞之前一点，然后推理模型显然改变了一切。我的意思是，你知道，从某种意义上说今天——你知道我们预览了产品——它看起来确实不错——预览我们私下看的，但我们会把视频放到 YouTube 上——它基本上就是给律师用的 ChatGPT，对吧？这么说很公平。但侧边栏有很多不错的自定义工具，比如表格视图，比如我很喜欢的 Intake，还有你知道的一堆其他东西。

turns.en: Exactly, that's exactly what it is. It's coworker ChatGPT is like really really good for legal and the workflow for like in-house corporate lawyers, people looking for upcoming regulations, all these things, and we can talk about more of the products there.
turns.zh: 没错，就是这样。它就是同事版 ChatGPT，对法律工作真的非常非常好，对于像内部公司律师、寻找即将出台的法规的人，所有这些事情，我们可以多聊聊那里的产品。

turns.en: Yeah. What models are you guys using underneath? Like can you talk about that?
turns.zh: 对。你们底层用的是什么模型？能聊聊吗？

turns.en: I mean, we're using a bunch of different ones depending on task, right? That's um—
turns.zh: 我的意思是，我们根据任务使用一堆不同的模型，对吧？那是——

turns.en: And then that's not available to the lawyer to see you guys?
turns.zh: 那律师看不到你们用的这些？

turns.en: For the—yeah. Well, we've been back and forth on this. Yeah.
turns.zh: 对于——是的。嗯，我们在这件事上反复讨论过。是的。

turns.en: Just like everyone else, I think in the agent there's a model selector for the primary model, but there are certain tools where we use different models. There's tabular view, and we try— I think we found it most effective to subdivide the problem and route as we subdivide the task. But we do right now have a picker in the agent. I'm not sure if that's going to stay there always, to be honest. So yeah.
turns.zh: 和所有人一样，我认为智能体里有一个针对主模型的选择器，但有些工具我们会用不同的模型。比如表格视图，我们尝试——我觉得最有效的做法是把问题细分，在细分任务的同时做路由。不过我们现在确实在智能体里放了一个选择器。说实话，我不确定它会不会一直留在那里。所以是的。

turns.en: Yeah. I mean, I bring a little bit of context to this because I'm an adviser for Cognition.
turns.zh: 是的。我补充一点背景，因为我是 Cognition 的顾问。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And when I joined, you know, part of my thesis for what an agent lab is— an agent lab is, ideally, a domain-specific GPT wrapper, right? We run the— we are the domain experts. We'll pay attention to you. We'll serve your needs way, way more than the frontier labs, and we'll give you the best of the frontier labs according to our judgment. So our job is to decide for you, because your job is not to—
turns.zh: 我刚加入的时候，我对智能体实验室是什么的一部分论点是——智能体实验室理想上就是一个领域专用的 GPT 套壳，对吧？我们负责运营——我们是领域专家。我们会关注你，比前沿实验室更好地服务你的需求，并按照我们的判断把前沿实验室最好的东西给你。所以我们的工作是替你决定，因为你的工作不是——

turns.en: Exactly. We'll always keep you on the PTO frontier and make sure that it's great all the time, and you don't have to dive into all the details. Because one of the things— to this point, if you go to a lawyer and you ask them, oh, you're going to draft this contract based on this precedent, do you think that's a Sonnet-high or an Opus-mid task? You know, they won't know. Just give me this—
turns.zh: 正是如此。我们会一直让你处在 PTO 前沿，确保它始终很棒，你不需要深入所有细节。因为有一点——说到这个，如果你去找律师，问他们：哦，你要根据这个先例起草这份合同，你觉得这是 Sonnet 高配还是 Opus 中配的任务？你知道，他们不会知道的。就给我这个——

turns.en: Just like make sure it works.
turns.zh: 就确保它能用。

turns.en: Hourly rate is $1,000 an hour.
turns.zh: 时薪 1000 美元。

turns.en: Exactly, just like make it work.
turns.zh: 没错，就让它能用就行。

turns.en: So yes, I originally came in with that. I was like, oh yeah, this is what Devon does differently. And now we have five things in the model picker, including Fable and Opus and Astra. And people want to experiment with the fancy new model.
turns.zh: 所以是的，我最初是带着这个想法来的。我当时想，哦对，这就是 Devon 与众不同的地方。而现在我们的模型选择器里有五个选项，包括 Fable、Opus 和 Astra。人们想试试那些花哨的新模型。

turns.en: Do you— is that the same?
turns.zh: 你觉得——情况一样吗？

turns.en: I think so. I think it's pro— it's definitely way less in legal than it is in engineering.
turns.zh: 我觉得是的。我觉得这——在法律领域肯定比工程领域少得多。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: But there are definitely people that just want table one right away. And you know, people were asking us about Mythos and everything. Even though I think realistically a lot of legal work does not require Mythos-level intelligence.
turns.zh: 但确实有人就想马上用 Table 1。你知道，人们一直在问我们 Mythos 之类的东西。尽管我认为现实中很多法律工作并不需要 Mythos 级别的智能。

turns.en: Yeah. So, exactly right. Like I think basically you're like, okay, we'll give you the option. You asked for this, but you're going to run down your credits like 10x faster than—
turns.zh: 是的。所以完全正确。我觉得基本上你就是说，好吧，我们给你这个选项。你要求了，但你的额度会消耗得快 10 倍——

turns.en: Yeah. I would have loved— we fought introducing it for a very long time, and then in the end we just kind of caved in. We're like, okay, if you want this level of control, then we'll give it to you.
turns.zh: 是的。我本来很想——我们抗拒引入它很久，最后我们还是妥协了。我们说，好吧，如果你想要这种程度的控制，那我们就给你。

turns.en: Yeah. So, you think the models are already like as good as lawyers need? Like there's no need for them to get better.
turns.zh: 是的。所以你觉得模型已经达到律师需要的水平了？就是没必要再变强了？

turns.en: It's a— I think it's a power distribution. So there's probably like 60% of the work we can do really well right now, and from now on it's a cost and latency thing. But then there's the rest of the thing where, especially for very complex analysis, we still need more intelligence. And then I think there's also just the work expansion— kind of like that's the work that we have right now, but also the work of a lord— thus probably expands with intelligence, I imagine.
turns.zh: 这是——我觉得这是一个能力分布。大概 60% 的工作我们现在就能做得很好，从现在起就是成本和延迟的问题。但剩下的部分，尤其是非常复杂的分析，我们仍然需要更多智能。然后我觉得还有工作范围的扩张——就像我们现在有这些工作，但律师的工作大概也会随着智能而扩张，我想。

turns.en: Early on, like when you guys first started, I guess transitioning to the agents or building the agents, like what models were you guys using? I guess it would have been like Opus 4.6 or something.
turns.zh: 早期，你们刚开始的时候，我猜是转向智能体或者构建智能体的时候，你们用的是什么模型？我猜大概是 Opus 4.6 之类的。

turns.en: That would have been— yeah. Sonnet 4.6. Opus 4.6 is probably right.
turns.zh: 那应该是——是的。Sonnet 4.6。Opus 4.6 大概没错。

turns.en: What were the agents not good at at that point that they're much better at now, even though it's only what, like 9 months later?
turns.zh: 那时候智能体不擅长、但现在强得多的是什么，尽管才过了大概 9 个月？

turns.en: Sub-agent delegation was one of them that we've gotten working really well now. For fan-out type retrieval queries it works extremely well for us now. That was difficult before.
turns.zh: 子智能体委派是其中之一，我们现在已经让它运转得很好了。对于扇出型检索查询，现在对我们来说效果极好。以前这很难。

turns.en: We basically track— so we have a team that's just doing evals. And so we track all of the models' performance in different practice areas, which is like subgroups of legal, and different tasks across all those. So we basically have a big heat map, and we're like—
turns.zh: 我们基本上会追踪——我们有一个专门做评估的团队。所以我们追踪所有模型在不同执业领域的表现，也就是法律的不同子领域，以及这些领域里的不同任务。所以我们基本上有一张大的热力图，然后我们——

turns.en: And then we can see them move, and usually they improve most stuff, but there are actually a lot of model releases where they improve some and regress in others.
turns.zh: 然后我们能看到它们的变化，通常它们会改善大部分东西，但实际上有很多模型发布是改善了一些、在另一些上退步了。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: And that actually happens a lot more than you'd think.
turns.zh: 而这实际上比你想象的要常见得多。

turns.en: Like what are some of those tasks? Are you familiar with how you guys are running a lot of the evals, like what are those different subsegments, I guess, that you look at?
turns.zh: 比如那些任务是什么？你熟悉你们怎么跑这些评估吗，比如你们看的那些不同子领域是什么？

turns.en: Yeah. So there's different just like framing stuff. So we have different basically like worlds— like RL environments essentially— which is like, here's a— because lawyers work in projects always, more or less. So it's like, here's a 10,000-file data room. You're doing a due diligence, and in the end a grit report looks like this. It contains all these red flags, and it doesn't contain whatever weird stuff, and we want it to be concise, etc., etc. That's kind of how we've built it. So there's different tasks, which is like part of it is drafting a report: does the draft look good? Does it contain all the right stuff? Is the wording sound, the analysis sound? There's also the part of finding the red flags, like the analysis before that. So we can kind of subdivide it a little bit, and that's how we run the evals.
turns.zh: 是的。所以有不同种类的框架设定。我们基本上有不同的世界——本质上就是强化学习环境——就像，这里有一个——因为律师总是在做项目，或多或少。所以就像，这里有一个一万个文件的数据室。你在做尽职调查，最后一份 grit 报告长这样。它包含所有这些红旗警示，不包含那些奇怪的东西，我们希望它简洁，等等。我们大概就是这样构建的。所以有不同任务，其中一部分是起草报告：草稿看起来好吗？它包含所有正确的内容吗？措辞合理吗，分析合理吗？还有找红旗警示的部分，就是在那之前的分析。所以我们可以稍微细分一下，我们就是这样跑评估的。

turns.en: Interesting. Wait, what does your eval team look like? Like do you hire lawyers to like do that?
turns.zh: 有意思。等等，你们的评估团队是什么样的？你们会雇律师来做这个吗？

turns.en: So yes, it's a mix. We have engineers and then we have lawyers, and it's one team. So there's like three engineers and like three lawyers right now. And then we have a pool of what we call legal engineers, which is people that have worked in big law for like three or four years, typically maybe they have a CS degree, and they're very tech forward, and then they come to us because they want to help change the industry.
turns.zh: 是的，是混合的。我们有工程师，也有律师，是一个团队。现在大概有三个工程师和三个律师。然后我们有一个池子，我们称之为法律工程师，就是那些在大律所工作了大概三四年的人，通常他们可能有计算机学位，非常懂技术，然后他们来找我们，因为他们想帮助改变这个行业。

turns.en: Are they in big law or lawyers in big law?
turns.zh: 他们是在大律所，还是大律所的律师？

turns.en: They're lawyers in big law.
turns.zh: 他们是大型律所的律师。

turns.en: With CS degrees.
turns.zh: 还有计算机学位。

turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Oh my god. It's a Venn diagram. Yeah. Exactly.
turns.zh: 我的天。这是个维恩图。是的。没错。

turns.en: That's like our hardest person to hire for. But they're also such a force multiplier, because we can pull on them for the eval stuff and for the product development, which is like— you have a pool of 100 experts that use the product every day and go and talk to clients every day, and also like they live this and have lived this, and we just pull on them to do evals and help us shape the product. And it's such an advantage.
turns.zh: 那大概是我们最难招的人。但他们也是巨大的力量倍增器，因为我们可以拉他们来做评估和产品开发，就像——你有一个 100 名专家的池子，他们每天使用产品、每天和客户交谈，而且他们亲身经历并一直经历着这些，我们就拉他们来做评估、帮我们塑造产品。这真是巨大的优势。

turns.en: And curious, like when did you guys start that team?
turns.zh: 我很好奇，你们什么时候开始组建那个团队的？

turns.en: Evals grew out of the assistant agent team at some point. I think there was a point up until recently where it was like honestly just not really worth it, because all models just got better.
turns.zh: 评估在某个时候是从助手智能体团队里长出来的。我觉得直到最近，有一段时间它老实说并不太值得做，因为所有模型都在变好。

turns.en: So it was like, do we want to spend a lot of our time doing really complex evals, or do we just want to build? Because there was so much to be gained from building a better harness and just leaning into everything's going to improve. And everything kind of just improved.
turns.zh: 所以当时的问题是：我们是花大量时间做非常复杂的评估，还是直接去构建？因为构建更好的测试框架能带来很多收益，而且我们相信一切都会变好。结果一切确实都变好了。

turns.en: But yeah, like every 2-3 months you get just pass it through. Right.

Um and I think a really core thing is like how can we empower our legal engineers like how can we empower our power users and our legal engineers to customize the product in a powerful way. And then of course we we'll still have forward deploy engineers like help out you know do all the custom integrations and the scoping and figuring out what's possible and feed all that back into core product development. So that's kind of how I think about it. It's like almost a first line second line defense whereas like legal engineers should be able to customize a lot of stuff and build a great experience and then where they can't or we need to make core product changes or custom integrations or whatever. We have four deployed engineers who also then cycle in a little bit behind like sometimes they'll just work on the product and sometimes they'll work with clients.
turns.zh: 不，工程师，但我们做这个。我思考的一件事是如何在规模上实现这一点。嗯，我认为一个真正核心的事情是如何赋能我们的法律工程师，如何赋能我们的高级用户和法律工程师以强大的方式定制产品。然后当然我们仍然会有前置部署工程师来帮忙，你知道，做所有的自定义集成和范围界定，弄清楚什么是可能的，并把所有这些反馈到核心产品开发中。所以这就是我的思考方式。这几乎像第一线第二线防御，而法律工程师应该能够定制很多东西并构建出色的体验，然后在他们不能的地方，或者我们需要进行核心产品更改或自定义集成或其他什么。我们有四个部署工程师，他们也会在后面稍微轮换，有时他们只是做产品，有时他们与客户合作。

turns.en: Can you walk through an example? Like, okay, you just got this new client. What's step number one? Are you guys like, okay, hey, we have a forward deployed engineer for you guys. They're gonna go build some kind of product for you. Like, how does that work?
turns.zh: 你能走一遍一个例子吗？比如，好，你刚接到这个新客户。第一步是什么？你们是不是就说，嘿，我们给你派一位前驻工程师。他会去为你构建某种产品。这具体是怎么运作的？

turns.en: So it's very different client to client, right? But if it's a big client and they're super engaged and they have all these dreams of things they would want to do, or typically they've already tried to build something and it's failed, and they're like, this is a problem that we'd like to solve. Then we'll basically staff them with legal engineers and a forward deployed engineer, potentially, depending on what the thing is. And then we'll just be like, hey, these guys will come, they'll make you successful. They will sit with all your lawyers and teach them how to use it and figure out all the workflows that you have right now and build them into Lora. And some of that will just be a legal engineer, and some of that will require a forward deployed engineer.
turns.zh: 每个客户的情况差别很大，对吧？但如果是个大客户，而且他们非常投入，脑子里有一堆想做的事，或者通常他们已经尝试过构建某个东西但失败了，然后他们说，这是我们要解决的问题。那我们基本上会给他们配法律工程师，视情况可能再加一位前驻工程师。然后我们就说，嘿，这些人会过来，他们会让你成功。他们会和你的所有律师坐在一起，教他们怎么用，梳理出你现有的所有工作流，并把它们构建进 Lora。其中一部分只需要法律工程师，另一部分则需要前驻工程师。

ts.sec: Legal Engineer vs Forward Deployed Engineer

turns.en: What is that separation? I guess if you could talk about that a little bit.
turns.zh: 这个分工是什么？能不能稍微讲讲？

turns.en: Legal engineers configure the product as a power user would.
turns.zh: 法律工程师像高级用户那样配置产品。

turns.en: They don't write code.
turns.zh: 他们不写代码。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah.
turns.zh: 对，对。

turns.en: And a forward deployed engineer writes code into production, basically. I guess that's the—that's the—
turns.zh: 而前驻工程师基本上是把代码写进生产环境。我想这就是——这就是——

turns.en: What kind of background do the forward deployed engineers normally have? You said founder.
turns.zh: 前驻工程师通常是什么背景？你刚才说创始人。

turns.en: Yeah, founders, regular engineers, they're old.
turns.zh: 对，创始人、普通工程师，他们资历都比较老。

turns.en: Yeah. D was your—
turns.zh: 对。D 是你的——

turns.en: Yeah, exactly. D was our first. Yeah. Two YC companies and worked on search at Meta.
turns.zh: 对，没错。D 是我们的第一位。对。做过两家 YC 公司，在 Meta 做过搜索。

turns.en: Yeah. She's awesome. Yeah. Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。她很厉害。对，对。

turns.en: She's great. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. First boots on the ground in the US.
turns.zh: 她很棒。对，对，对，对，对。是我们在美国的第一批落地人员。

turns.en: Okay. That's a high bar.
turns.zh: 好。这个门槛很高。

turns.en: So what are some examples of, I don't know, workflows or things that these people are building for the clients? Do you guys have like, oh, these are a couple use cases that all the law firms are—you know, this is the first thing that our FDEs are going to do when they go in?
turns.zh: 那能举些例子吗？比如这些人为客户构建的工作流或东西？你们是不是有那种，哦，这几个用例是所有律所都会有的——你知道，这是我们的前驻工程师进去后要做的第一件事？

turns.en: It's very different. Some core workflows everyone has and we can just build in Lora, and that could be anything from, like, this is how we handle these types of NDAs or whatever, and it's just like you activate it. And it's more like skill building, really, for at least most of the FDEs. That's more like—
turns.zh: 差别很大。有些核心工作流每个人都有，我们可以直接构建进 Lora，可能是，比如，我们是这样处理这类保密协议的，诸如此类，你激活它就行。对至少大多数前驻工程师来说，这更像是技能构建。那更像是——

turns.en: There's something that we can't do yet, like we need some more flexibility in some of the primitives or whatever it might be, or we just have this really complex system that we need to integrate into. And then they'll go out there and they'll build the integration against our APIs and maybe expand our APIs or whatever to make that work.
turns.zh: 有些事我们还做不到，比如我们需要在某些基础组件上有更多灵活性，或者随便什么情况，或者我们有个非常复杂的系统需要集成进去。那他们就会出去，基于我们的 API 构建集成，也许还会扩展我们的 API 或别的什么，让这件事跑通。

turns.en: And how does the legal structure work there? Because you said you guys yourselves can't even work on deals. Yes. So like how do they work on client projects?
turns.zh: 那法律结构上是怎么运作的？因为你说过你们自己都不能处理交易。对。那他们怎么参与客户项目？

turns.en: You mean the law firms, how do they work on client projects?
turns.zh: 你是说律所，他们怎么参与客户项目？

turns.en: How do your FDEs work on client projects if they—
turns.zh: 你们的前驻工程师怎么参与客户项目，如果他们——

turns.en: So they don't touch the data still. So they'll just build the system. But they will also be onboarded like an employee sometimes. So like they might get a laptop and everything to—yeah. Yeah. If they need to.
turns.zh: 他们仍然不碰数据。所以他们只是构建系统。但有时候他们也会像员工一样被入职。比如他们可能会拿到一台笔记本电脑之类的——对。对。如果需要的话。

turns.en: Interesting. That doesn't happen very often because usually they'll just build an integration and it kind of works, but they—yeah, they can if they need to.
turns.zh: 有意思。这不太常发生，因为通常他们只是构建一个集成，差不多就能用了，但他们——对，如果需要的话可以。

turns.en: And you only onboard FTEs into a customer, I'm assuming, if they're a certain size.
turns.zh: 我猜只有当客户达到一定规模时，你们才会把全职员工入职到客户那边。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. It needs to make sense, 'cause FDEs can also work on core product, right? So it's like it's a constant prioritization thing.
turns.zh: 对。对。这得说得通，因为前驻工程师也可以做核心产品，对吧？所以这是个持续的优先级排序问题。

turns.en: Is there a rule like—I guess does every—so Palantir famously had like, you know, four days you spend on site, one day you come back and contribute back to products. Anything like that?
turns.zh: 有没有什么规则，比如——我猜是不是每个——Palantir  famously 有过那种，你知道，四天待在客户现场，一天回来给产品做贡献。有类似这样的吗？

turns.en: No, we don't. I mean, to be fully honest with you guys, it's still early days in a lot of this.
turns.zh: 没有，我们没有。说实话，很多这方面都还处在早期。

turns.en: Where do you see it headed? Maybe over the next year.
turns.zh: 你觉得它会往哪走？也许未来一年。

turns.en: I do think that it's going to be more—maybe not exactly like Palantir, but I think we will have a larger in-constant-circulation group of FDEs that maybe we sit with a client for like two months or whatever to build out this one thing, and then they go to the next one, etc., etc. Yeah, but I do imagine us rolling in with legal engineers and forward deployed engineers to work on specific projects.
turns.zh: 我确实认为会更——也许不完全像 Palantir，但我认为我们会有一个更大的、持续轮转的前驻工程师团队，也许我们在一个客户那里待两个月左右来构建这个东西，然后他们去下一个，等等等等。对，但我确实设想我们会带着法律工程师和前驻工程师进驻，去做特定项目。

ts.sec: API Strategy and Platform vs Product

turns.en: Yeah, the API business is actually interesting, like you said, because you know that's another role that you can have where—
turns.zh: 对，API 业务其实很有意思，就像你说的，因为你知道那是你可以有的另一个角色，其中——

turns.en: You are CTO maintainer of the Lora platform.
turns.zh: 你是 Lora 平台的首席技术官兼维护者。

turns.en: Right. Like we will offer everything that we have in the Lora web app as an API and then you guys can use whatever.
turns.zh: 对。比如我们会把 Lora 网页应用里的所有东西都作为 API 提供，然后你们想用什么就用什么。

turns.en: Is that—is that a promise that you make or—
turns.zh: 那是——那是你们做出的承诺吗，还是——

turns.en: That's not something we're promising now. We do have APIs that you can build against, but not the entire surface of the product.
turns.zh: 那不是我们现在承诺的事。我们确实有可以基于其构建的 API，但不是产品的全部界面。

turns.en: That's the curious thing. Like, is that the strategy? And obviously some people will love it because I don't have to learn a new tool. I can just use the existing tool I have, right? And then I just like—
turns.zh: 这就是有意思的地方。比如，那是策略吗？显然有些人会喜欢，因为我不用学新工具。我可以直接用我现有的工具，对吧？然后我就——

turns.en: Install Lora, for example, with the Word document stuff.
turns.zh: 比如把 Lora 装进 Word 文档那套东西里。

turns.en: Other than that, you know, I do think like then you have to maintain it.
turns.zh: 除此之外，你知道，我确实认为那你就得维护它。

turns.en: Exactly. That's so—that's been my thing. That's why we've tried not to do it. We haven't—we haven't had APIs. I mean, we started our APIs like six months ago or something. We fought it for a very long time. Mostly because, yeah, I just don't want to—we move so quickly in the product that I don't want to be slowed down by having to maintain old API versions for a data model that we've changed. I mean, now we're bigger and things are different. So now it's a cost that we can take on. But like when we're 20 engineers, it's just like we move so quickly that we can't do this.
turns.zh: 没错。这就是——这就是我一直的想法。这就是为什么我们尽量不做。我们一直没——我们一直没有 API。我是说，我们大概六个月前才开始做 API。我们抗拒了很久。主要因为，对，我就是不想——我们在产品上迭代太快了，我不想因为要为我们已经改过的数据模型维护旧版 API 而被拖慢。我是说，现在我们更大了，情况不同了。所以现在这是我们可以承担的成本。但当我们只有 20 个工程师时，我们迭代太快了，做不了这个。

turns.en: I've toyed with this, right? Like it's just generally good for all companies to have a platform team and a product team, because the product team you have one, but then you can easily spin up a second one as long as the platform is not super tight to product.
turns.zh: 我琢磨过这个，对吧？比如一般来说，所有公司都有平台团队和产品团队是好事，因为产品团队你有一个，但只要平台和产品不是绑得太死，你很容易再开第二个。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: You know, like a very simple one is web app, mobile app, right? Or like web app, mobile app, API, and then like whatever other integrations. Then your FDEs just are one more client to the overall platform anyway.
turns.zh: 你知道，很简单的一个例子就是网页应用、移动应用，对吧？或者网页应用、移动应用、API，然后随便什么其他集成。那你的前驻工程师反正也只是整个平台的又一个客户而已。

turns.en: Yes. Yeah. And I think like even the agent you can think about it this way. There's like a harness team or like a—that runs the agent, and then you can even build a product around it with like skills and automations and whatever else.
turns.zh: 对。对。而且我觉得连智能体也可以这么看。有一个类似运行框架的团队，或者说运行智能体的东西，然后你甚至可以围绕它构建产品，加上技能、自动化之类的。

ts.sec: API Mandate and Agent as API

turns.en: Yeah, this is very famously the Amazon Web Services mandate. Bezos was like, no more backdoor access. You only offer other teams your APIs, the same APIs you offer customers. If you don't have it, you build it.
turns.zh: 对，这就是非常著名的亚马逊云服务（AWS）指令。贝索斯说，不能再有后门访问。你只能向其他团队提供你的 API，也就是你向客户提供的同一套 API。如果没有，你就自己建。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: And then the customers also get it.
turns.zh: 然后客户也能拿到。

turns.en: Yeah. I think that's also changing a little bit. A lot of APIs now — one thing that we're toying with is, can the agent be the API? I know it sounds weird, but for some of this stuff, what they actually want to do is they want to trigger certain things to happen. For some part of this, you could just be — I'm not saying that we're doing this, but it's a thing that I'm toying with in my head — could that just be like, okay, you trigger the agent and ask it to do this thing? Obviously it's way less efficient than if you just had an API that you always hit. But it's something that I'm toying with: how much of our product can just be the agent versus all the other stuff.
turns.zh: 对。我觉得这一点也在发生一些变化。现在很多 API——我们正在琢磨的一件事是：智能体能不能就是 API？我知道这听起来很奇怪，但对某些东西来说，他们真正想要的是触发某些事情发生。对其中一部分来说，你可以直接——我不是说我们在这么做，但这是我脑子里在琢磨的事——能不能就是，好，你触发智能体，让它去做这件事？显然，这比有一个你总是调用的 API 效率低得多。但我在琢磨的是：我们的产品里有多少可以直接就是智能体，而不是其他那些东西。

turns.en: Well, you know, unbounded execution and cost and latency.
turns.zh: 嗯，你知道，无限制的执行、成本和延迟。

turns.en: That's the — is that the only holdback?
turns.zh: 这就是——这是唯一的阻碍吗？

turns.en: That's — yeah. And then I think determinism. Like maybe two out of 100 times it's going to do something whack that we didn't want it to do.
turns.zh: 这是——对。然后我觉得还有确定性。也许 100 次里有 2 次，它会做一些我们不希望它做的离谱事情。

turns.en: We're going to go into harness and model fine-tuning in a bit. But I think there's a product question about restraint — what you don't do — because you could do all that. And obviously there's a prioritization issue. Like, are you more at a point of, let's say no to most things and only do a short number of stuff? Or no, actually we want to do more things and we just need to hire like 100 people?
turns.zh: 我们待会儿会聊到 harness 和模型微调。但我觉得有一个关于克制——也就是你不做什么——的产品问题，因为那些你都可以做。显然还有优先级问题。比如，你现在更倾向于对大多数事情说不，只做少数几件事？还是说，不，其实我们想做更多事，只是需要再招 100 个人？

turns.en: I was very strongly the first thing for a very long time. Let's just say no to everything. Keep the eng team — I think I've said this before — one of our presentations, after I'd been at Liora for half a year, I pulled up this slide of the 300 Spartans from the movie and I was like, we're just going to be 20 engineers for the rest of the company's history and we're going to beat everyone who's much bigger. And we're 100 engineers now and it feels like we're way too small. I wanted to do that, but I think in the real world we're in fierce competition. People want so much stuff. I could be a Puritan and just be like, no, we have to stay 20 people and we can only build whatever. But then we just lose and people would go elsewhere. So we have to build more. And so I think my job is to figure out how do I build a system where we can build a lot but actually only — where the customer feels like we've built so much stuff but we've actually only built a few things. That's how I think about my job right now.
turns.zh: 很长一段时间里，我非常强烈地倾向于第一种。就对一切说不。保持工程团队——我想我以前说过——我们有一次演示，我在 Liora 待了半年后，翻出电影《300 勇士》的那张幻灯片，我说，公司剩下的历史里我们就只做 20 个工程师，我们要打败所有比我们大得多的公司。现在我们已经有 100 个工程师了，感觉还是太小。我本想那样做，但我觉得在现实世界里，我们面临激烈的竞争。人们想要太多东西。我可以做个清教徒，就说不行，我们必须保持 20 个人，我们只能做某某东西。但那样我们就输了，人们会去别处。所以我们必须做更多。所以我觉得我的工作是弄清楚，如何建立一个系统，让我们能做很多，但实际上只——让客户觉得我们做了很多东西，而我们实际上只做了少数几件事。这就是我现在对自己工作的理解。

turns.en: Yeah. I mean, primitives is right, you know.
turns.zh: 对。我是说，原语（primitives）是对的，你知道。

turns.en: Yeah. Exactly. I think that's going to be really powerful.
turns.zh: 对。没错。我觉得那会非常强大。

turns.en: Do you test new products, just seeing if there's any pull here, and then you're like, no, let's just focus on our main thing? Or —
turns.zh: 你们会测试新产品，看看这里有没有需求，然后你说，不，我们还是专注主业？还是——

turns.en: We haven't made — I mean, we've made certain strategic bets, but we've not tried anything that we don't have a lot of confidence in already. Mostly because we just have a mountain of demand — like, we want all of these things — and so it hasn't really made sense for us to try to be like, hey, maybe this thing could work, because there's so many people screaming for the other things. So we mostly build those. And then sometimes we'll disagree with clients and we'll be like, actually I think this thing over here will make a lot of sense strategically, and then we'll try to build that anyway.
turns.zh: 我们还没有——我是说，我们做过一些战略押注，但我们没试过任何我们本来就不太有信心的事。主要是因为我们有堆积如山的需求——比如，这些东西我们都想要——所以去试“嘿，也许这个东西能行”对我们来说并不太合理，因为有那么多人在为其他东西呼喊。所以我们主要做那些。然后有时我们会不同意客户，我们会说，其实我觉得这边这个东西在战略上会很有意义，然后我们还是会试着去做它。

turns.en: Like strategically for you.
turns.zh: 比如对你们来说有战略意义。

turns.en: Yeah, exactly.
turns.zh: 对，没错。

turns.en: So what are those things?
turns.zh: 那那些东西是什么？

turns.en: So one of those things was the agent actually. No one was actually asking for — like, I want the assistant that I'm using to have more agency and do things without me asking it. No one ever. But we were just like, this is definitely where the industry is going. This is going to empower you to do so much cool stuff. Collaboration was another one, where we think the industry is going to a place where you can collaborate inside of where you're working, which is Liora, and not in emails and text messages. So yeah, there are a few of those.
turns.zh: 其中一件事其实就是智能体。其实没人要求——比如“我想让我用的助手有更多自主性，不用我问就做事”。从来没人提过。但我们就是觉得，这绝对是行业的走向。这会让你能做很多很酷的事。协作是另一个，我们认为行业正走向一个地方，让你可以在你工作的地方——也就是 Liora——里面协作，而不是在邮件和短信里。所以对，有那么几件。

turns.en: And then how — once you say, okay, we want you guys to use agents, I'm assuming internally at the law firm it's going to take a lot for them to actually learn how to do that. And so that's where you kind of say, hey, FDEs, go in there and teach them what they —
turns.zh: 然后怎么——一旦你说，好，我们希望你们用智能体，我猜在律所内部，他们要真正学会怎么做需要花很多功夫。所以这就是你说，嘿，FDE（前向部署工程师），进去教他们——

turns.en: Yeah. Legal engineers mostly, but some people call them forward-deployed legal engineers if you want, but that's essentially what they are. Then they go in and help them structure their workflows around the capabilities of the agent.
turns.zh: 对。主要是法律工程师，但有人愿意的话叫他们前向部署法律工程师，但本质上就是那样。然后他们进去，帮助他们围绕智能体的能力来组织工作流。

turns.en: You guys said previously — I think Max said this — that early on, specifically, you guys weren't fine-tuning your own models. Is that still the case?

I think if you're a big enterprise, you might have Claude co-work and then you'll—I think it's similar to how I use Linear through Claude but I still go to Linear. I think enterprise will do that. I think law firms will just use Legora because that's simpler and better.
turns.zh: 我觉得两者都会有。这真的取决于情况。我觉得如果你是大企业，你可能会用 Claude 协作，然后你会——我觉得这类似于我通过 Claude 用 Linear，但我还是会去 Linear。我觉得企业会那样做。我觉得律所会直接用 Legora，因为那更简单也更好。

turns.en: It kind of reminds me of OpenEvidence for medicine. You're basically that for law.
turns.zh: 这让我想起医学领域的 OpenEvidence。你基本上就是法律领域的那个。

turns.en: Exactly.
turns.zh: 没错。

turns.en: In coding, it's gotten to a point where the labs will cut you off for competing with them, and this has happened twice. Do you think that will happen to law?
turns.zh: 在编程领域，事情已经到了实验室会因为你和他们竞争而切断你的地步，这已经发生过两次了。你觉得法律领域会发生这种事吗？

turns.en: No, I don't think so. I think because, you know, they are releasing legal services, right? They are—
turns.zh: 不，我不这么认为。我觉得因为，你知道，他们也在推出法律服务，对吧？他们在——

turns.en: I don't—I mean, we obviously talk to them a lot, but it's also like, hey, are you going to—
turns.zh: 我不——我是说，我们显然经常和他们聊，但也会问，嘿，你们会不会——

turns.en: Your sales reps will say no. They don't make the call. Exactly. That's not their right. And they don't even know often what's actually going on. I don't think that's the case. They have so much stuff to capture in knowledge work or in enterprise knowledge work generally that legal has to be part of that, just like data analytics has to, and sales and marketing and finance. So they have to do things that are good there, but they're never going to go as deep as we are. And I think if Claude takes small client, small corporate clients, and they do some of their legal via Claude, like that's great. That's fine. But if you're doing a $400 million M&A transaction, you're going to want Legora.
turns.zh: 你们的销售代表会说不会。他们不做决定。没错。那不是他们的职权。而且他们往往甚至不知道实际发生了什么。我不认为会那样。他们在知识工作，或者说企业知识工作里，有太多东西要覆盖，法律必然是其中一部分，就像数据分析必然是，销售、营销和财务也是。所以他们必须把那些做好，但他们永远不会像我们做得那么深。我觉得如果 Claude 拿下小客户、小企业客户，他们通过 Claude 处理一些法律事务，那很好，没问题。但如果你在做一笔 4 亿美元的并购交易，你会想要 Legora。

turns.en: I had kind of an unrelated question, but I'm curious. Are you guys going to law schools and getting them to teach Legora in classes? Like how does that work?
turns.zh: 我有个不太相关的问题，但我很好奇。你们会去法学院，让他们在课堂上教 Legora 吗？这具体是怎么运作的？

turns.en: It's definitely a program that we have started. I actually don't know exactly where we are, but we do want people in law school to learn to use Legora.
turns.zh: 这肯定是我们已经启动的一个项目。我其实不太清楚我们具体进展到哪了，但我们确实希望法学院的人学会用 Legora。

turns.en: Like, are you seeing that law schools are changing their curriculums a lot or not really?
turns.zh: 比如，你看到法学院在大幅调整课程设置吗，还是并没有？

turns.en: I don't know. I wouldn't know actually.
turns.zh: 我不知道。我其实不太清楚。

turns.en: Interesting.
turns.zh: 有意思。

turns.en: I would actually do it a different way. You should do scholarships for law school for CS majors, for engineers. We will cover your—after you've done CS, we'll put you in law school. CS plus some software experience, we'll put you in law school.
turns.zh: 我其实会换个方式做。你们应该为计算机专业、为工程师设立法学院奖学金。我们会覆盖你的——在你读完计算机之后，我们把你送进法学院。计算机加上一些软件经验，我们把你送进法学院。

turns.en: We'll cover it. Where you do like the MA or like master's plus JD programs.
turns.zh: 我们会覆盖。就是那种硕士加 JD 的项目。

turns.en: Yeah. You don't care about the master's.
turns.zh: 对。你不在乎那个硕士。

turns.en: Well, meaning like because there's a lot of people who didn't do CS undergrad, so then they do like masters just to kind of get caught up.
turns.zh: 嗯，意思是说，因为很多人本科没学计算机科学，所以就读个硕士，只是为了补上基础。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. I don't know. I don't see that as often.
turns.zh: 对，对。我不知道，我不太常见到这种情况。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah.
turns.zh: 对，对。

turns.en: People do JD-MBA. That's a thing.
turns.zh: 有人读法律博士加工商管理硕士，这是有的。

turns.en: But JD-CS, I haven't seen it. Yeah.
turns.zh: 但法律博士加计算机科学，我没见过。对。

turns.en: Happens. Yeah.
turns.zh: 也有。对。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. Okay. Look, overall, you know, super impressive progress. I mean, congrats on all your success. Like, are you still going to keep up the pace? Like, yeah. You know, and I think you're hiring in SF, New York.
turns.zh: 对，对。好，总的来说，你知道，进展非常惊人。我是说，恭喜你取得的所有成功。你还会保持这个节奏吗？对。而且我记得你们在旧金山、纽约招人。

turns.en: We're hiring in engineering. We're hiring in New York, Stockholm, and London.
turns.zh: 我们在招工程岗，在纽约、斯德哥尔摩和伦敦招人。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: And all other roles we're hiring everywhere.
turns.zh: 其他所有岗位我们也在各地招人。

turns.en: How many people do you have in New York right now?
turns.zh: 你们现在纽约有多少人？

turns.en: Okay. And you guys are planning on how many in New York?
turns.zh: 好。那你们计划在纽约招到多少人？

turns.en: In New York?
turns.zh: 在纽约？

turns.en: Yeah. For just like generally,
turns.zh: 对，就大概整体来说，

turns.en: let's just say, yeah, generally in
turns.zh: 就这么说吧，对，整体上

turns.en: um, a lot. As many as you can.
turns.zh: 嗯，很多。能招多少招多少。

turns.en: Yeah. And it's aggressive.
turns.zh: 对，而且这个目标很激进。

ts.sec: Legal as the frontier of knowledge work

turns.en: Yeah. I mean, well, that's the whole of corporate law, right, as far as America's concerned. So, like, yeah. I mean, I'm looking forward to you buying a law firm and, like, you know, becoming—
turns.zh: 对。我是说，就美国而言，整个公司法就是这样，对吧。所以，对。我是说，我很期待你们收购一家律所，然后，你知道，成为——

turns.en: Yeah. It's super exciting. I think, like, you know, every industry, especially like the top—like doctors, lawyers, coders—you know, they all have to have, like, you know, two or three agent labs that just completely dominate the space. So you guys have, like, a great market.
turns.zh: 对，这非常令人兴奋。我觉得，你知道，每个行业，尤其是顶尖的——医生、律师、程序员——你知道，他们都得有，你知道，两三家智能体实验室完全主导这个领域。所以你们有一个很棒的市场。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah, I think so. And I think it's only going to get much bigger as, like, law changes and becomes more available to more people.
turns.zh: 对，对，我也这么认为。而且我觉得随着法律变化、对更多人变得更可及，这个市场只会大得多。

turns.en: Yeah. Also, I think, I mean, we're already like super over—but like, the problems that you work on are very like the frontier of knowledge work, you know?
turns.zh: 对。另外我觉得，我是说，我们其实已经超级——但你做的这些问题非常处于知识工作的前沿，你知道吗？

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: There. Okay. Like unless you're literally like doing like science, Navier-Stokes and science, other than that, like most work is like basically converges to legal.
turns.zh: 就是这样。好。除非你真的在做科学，比如纳维-斯托克斯方程之类的科学，除此之外，大多数工作基本上都收敛到法律。

turns.en: Yeah. Like, yeah. Uh yeah, it's all legal in the end. Yeah. Hiring, finance, everything. Like I just have to consult my lawyer. So yeah, I know. I know. Which is why I think it's a really exciting thing to work on, cuz like modern society runs in some way on legal.
turns.zh: 对。就像，对。嗯对，最后都是法律。对。招聘、金融，一切。就像我只需要咨询我的律师。所以对，我知道，我知道。这就是为什么我觉得做这件事非常令人兴奋，因为现代社会在某种程度上是靠法律运转的。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah.
turns.zh: 对，对。

turns.en: Cool. All right, that's it. Thank you. Thank you. Thanks.
turns.zh: 好。行，就到这里。谢谢。谢谢。谢谢。

consensus.en: Legal AI will make lawyers more productive, shifting work to judgment and client relationships.
consensus.zh: 法律AI将提升律师生产力，使其工作转向判断和客户关系。

consensus.en: The partnership model may evolve as firms build durable intangible capital from codified expertise.
consensus.zh: 随着律所将专业知识编码为持久无形资产，合伙模式可能演变。

consensus.en: Billing is shifting from hourly to project-based fees, especially for lower-end work.
consensus.zh: 计费方式正从按小时转向按项目收费，尤其是低端工作。

consensus.en: Model routing and task subdivision are key to optimizing cost, latency, and quality.
consensus.zh: 模型路由和任务细分是优化成本、延迟和质量的关键。

consensus.en: Evals are crucial for tracking model performance across legal tasks and practice areas.
consensus.zh: 评估对于跟踪模型在法律任务和执业领域的表现至关重要。

consensus.en: Forward-deployed engineers and legal engineers help clients customize and adopt the product.
consensus.zh: 前置部署工程师和法律工程师帮助客户定制和采用产品。

contrarian.en: Most legal work doesn't require mythos-level intelligence; current models suffice for 60% of tasks.
contrarian.zh: 大多数法律工作不需要神话级智能；当前模型已能胜任60%的任务。

contrarian.en: Junior lawyers and paralegals aren't disappearing; good ones are worth more than before.
contrarian.zh: 初级律师和律师助理并未消失；优秀的比以往更有价值。

contrarian.en: Model releases often regress on some tasks, not just improve everywhere.
contrarian.zh: 模型发布常常在某些任务上退步，而非全面进步。

contrarian.en: You can't look at user traces due to confidentiality, so evals must approximate real work.
contrarian.zh: 由于保密性，无法查看用户轨迹，因此评估必须近似真实工作。

contrarian.en: The agent could become the API, replacing traditional deterministic APIs for some use cases.
contrarian.zh: 智能体可能成为API，在某些用例中取代传统的确定性API。

contrarian.en: Custom embeddings are essential; default embeddings leave significant performance on the table.
contrarian.zh: 自定义嵌入至关重要；默认嵌入会损失显著性能。
